subject: Post-call: POC environment options, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: POC environment options, success criteria & next steps

Hi Lina — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and a proposal to keep momentum:

Call highlights:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference latency/cost and data handling for PHI-backed Q&A workloads across a 4-week POC.
- Key constraints: Acme needs auditability + no PHI egress outside VPC if possible; limited infra calendar window in mid-Oct.
- Primary internal stakeholders: Lina (Product), infra team (cc).

Suggested POC approach (options):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted models in our secure hosted tenant. Pros: fastest to start (48–72h), lowest ops overhead. Cons: less isolation; not ideal for PHI.
2) Dedicated sandbox (recommended fall-back): dedicated GPU pool in Redwood Dedicated with isolated tenant and per-token billing. Pros: predictable throughput, quick spin-up (5–7 business days). Good for performance & cost proof.
3) VPC trial (preferred for PHI): Private deployment into Acme VPC / peered network. Pros: full network isolation and KMS control. Cons: longest lead time (2–4 weeks) for networking, IAM, and security approvals.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- P95 generation latency <= 400ms at 8 concurrent sessions.
- Token cost per 1k tokens <= $1.20 (budget placeholder — we'll refine).
- No PHI leaves the VPC. Evidence: audit logs + KV prefix cache controls.
- Quality: F1 >= 0.85 on your 200-case evaluation set (we'll import your test set).

Immediate next steps to align timelines:
- Lina & infra: indicate preferred environment (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC) by EOD Thu 9/10.
- Redwood (Rafael): produce a short ops checklist and an environment playbook (attach: redwood_poc_action_plan_v1.xlsx). Due: Mon 9/13.
- Acme: share the 200-case eval set and any compliance questionnaire items.

If you want the fastest path while compliance gets approved, we suggest starting in Dedicated sandbox and then migrating to VPC for the final 2 weeks of the POC — this provides performance/cost signals without stalling.

I attached a one-page action plan and SOC2 summary for your security team to review. If helpful, Rafael can run a technical pre-kickoff next week.

Proposed times for a short ops kickoff: Tue 9/14 or Wed 9/15 (30 min). Lina — does either work?

Thanks — look forward to your preference so we can lock dates.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment stubs: redwood_poc_action_plan_v1.xlsx (14 KB), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (220 KB)

- Two asks from infra/security: (1) SOC2 attestation + encryption/KMS details (we saw the summary but infra will need a short tech appendix), (2) estimated cost ranges for Dedicated vs VPC for a 4-week POC.

I can share the 200-case eval set by EOD Fri 9/10.

Scheduling: Wed 9/15 10:30 AM PT works for an infra kickoff (30 min). I added infra@acmehealth.com.

Thanks — we'll be ready to run a lightweight smoke test within 48h of Dedicated sandbox readiness.

Stephanie

Adding the tech checklist for the VPC pathway and estimated lead times (high level):

Tech checklist (VPC trial):
- Network peering or Transit Gateway configuration — Acme network team to open peering; Redwood to provide target CIDR and NAT recommendations. Lead time: 7–10 business days.
- IP allowlist & egress rules — Acme to supply allowed egress endpoints; Redwood to provide expected IP ranges. Lead time: 2–3 business days once details submitted.
- Certificate & KMS integration — If Acme wants customer-managed keys, we need KMS details (provider & ARN). Lead time: 3–5 business days to validate.
- Audit logging & SIEM hookup — Redwood will emit audit logs to a secure S3 or push to syslog; infra to confirm ingestion. Lead time: 3–7 business days.
- Load & perf baseline (non-PHI) in Dedicated sandbox — Redwood to run baseline test once sandbox is ready. Timeline: Sandbox ready in 5 business days; baseline within 48h.

Owners and contacts:
- Redwood: Rafael Mendes (tech lead) — rafael_mendes@redwood.com; Marissa Cole (trial ops) — marissa_cole@redwood.com.
- Acme: Lina Torres (product); infra@acmehealth.com (network).

Risk notes:
- If legal review for cross-account keys or KMS policy takes longer than 7 days, the VPC cutover may slip into late Oct.

Next steps:
- Rafael to upload a short "VPC tech appendix" (attached: vpc_network_requirements.md) and a SOC2 appendix (attached: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf).
- Marissa to propose Dedicated sandbox start date once Acme confirms a preferred kickoff (we will target 9/21 if infra can close peering by 9/20).

I'll be on the Wed 9/15 10:30 AM PT kickoff to walk infra through the checklist.

—
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
